program_name: Hospitality and Tourism Management (Master's Degree Course in Hospitality and Tourism Management; marketed to international applicants on apply.iulm.it as "MA Hospitality and Tourism Management - Dual Degree"). No Italian-language twin course exists; the Italian-language IULM pages use the same English title "Hospitality and Tourism Management".
teaching_language: Fully English-taught. The programme page states "The Programme is entirely delivered in English", and the apply.iulm.it course record gives "Study language: English". All admission tests are held in English ("written test in English", "The admissions test ... oral test"). There is no Italian-taught component of the curriculum. However, section 5 of the admission regulations imposes a separate Italian-language obligation that is NOT an entry condition but a graduation condition: candidates who are not native Italian speakers and/or non-Italian citizens must declare their Italian level when applying for the admission test and must obtain, by the end of their studies, a qualification attesting to written and oral proficiency in Italian.
campus: Milan (Milano) - IULM single campus, Via Carlo Bo 1, 20143 Milano. The second year may be spent abroad: the UCF track takes place in Orlando, Florida (Rosen College of Hospitality Management); the Oulu track spends the second semester of year two in Oulu, Finland; the third track stays at IULM Milan.
degree_class: LM-49 - Progettazione e gestione dei sistemi turistici, rendered in the English admission regulations as "LM-49 Planning and Management of Tourism Systems" and on the English programme page as "LM-49 - Design and management of tourism systems"
academic_requirements:
PLACES: 100 places for a.y. 2026/2027 ("1. Number of places available for the academic year 2026/2027 - 100 places"). The Italian-language version of the same admission regulations states the identical figure ("1. Posti disponibili per l'A.A. 2026/2027 - 100 posti"), and both the English and the Italian registration pages state 100 - so, unlike some other IULM programmes in this research, NO quota discrepancy exists between the English and Italian pages for this programme. The programme page classifies it as a "Course with scheduled number of places with selective knowledge testing".

CANDIDATE CATEGORIES: (a) internal graduates/undergraduates of the IULM Bachelor's in Tourism, Management and Culture (Turismo, management e cultura, and previous degree courses of the Faculty); (b) external graduates/undergraduates from other universities or from other IULM courses; (c) foreign graduates - "Italian or foreign citizens (EU and/or non-EU) in possession of a foreign admission qualification obtained in Italy or abroad", whose "Student records will be assessed on an individual basis". All categories must have graduated, or plan to graduate, by the autumn session of a.y. 2025/26, i.e. by 31 December 2026.

PRIOR QUALIFICATION: a first-cycle (Bachelor's) university degree, awarded or about to be awarded. apply.iulm.it gives the entry qualification as "Undergraduate diploma (or higher) Bachelor's degree", evaluated case by case; the general IULM master prerequisites page requires "a relevant and coherent Bachelor's degree diploma correspondent to EQF (European Qualification Framework) Level 6 and 180 ECTS or more".

CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (route 1 - degree class): the Bachelor's degree must belong to one of the following Italian classes, or be an equivalent foreign degree qualification: L-1 (Cultural Heritage), L-5 (Philosophy), L-6 (Geography), L-8 (Information Engineering), L-10 (Arts), L-11 (Modern Languages and Cultures), L-12 (Language Mediation), L-15 (Tourism), L-16 (Administration and Organisation), L-18 (Economics and Corporate Management), L-19 (Education and Training), L-20 (Communication), L-21 (Territorial, Urban, Landscape and Environmental Planning), L-31 (Information Technology), L-33 (Economics), L-37 (Social Sciences for Cooperation, Development and Peace), L-41 (Statistics), L-42 (History).

CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (route 2 - credits): candidates graduating in any other class must have acquired, or be about to acquire by the application deadline, at least 60 CFU/ECTS in one or more of these scientific-disciplinary sectors - IUS/07, IUS/09; L-LIN/12; SECS-P/01, P/02, P/03, P/05, P/06, P/07, P/08, P/09, P/10, P/11, P/13; SPS/01, SPS/04, SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/11, SPS/12; SECS-S/01 to S/06; MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/08, MAT/09; M-PSI/01, M-PSI/05, M-PSI/06; INF/01 - obtained in the three-year degree course, by passing single university courses, or by obtaining a university master's degree. (Note this list is identical to the Strategic Communication list except that ICAR/13 is not included here.)

EXCLUSIONS: "Applications will not be accepted from graduates from AFAM Institutes (Istituzioni di Alta Formazione Artistica, Musicale e Coreutica)." SSML (Scuole Superiori per Mediatori Linguistici) students/graduates are assessed on an individual basis; before applying online they must e-mail a detailed exam certificate to ammissioni.magistrali@iulm.it and may apply only after approval by the Coordinator for Master's Degree Courses.

RANKING CRITERIA: NOT PUBLISHED for this programme. Unlike other IULM master's admission regulations (e.g. Strategic Communication), the Hospitality and Tourism Management "Modalita ammissione LM HTM 2026_2027" PDF - checked in both its English and Italian versions - contains NO section on ranking lists, merit points derived from the Bachelor's degree grade or exam average, minimum CFU thresholds per session, per-session place allocation, tie-break rules, or a direct-admission/no-test route for internal candidates. Section 9 states only that candidates who have demonstrated English at B2 "will be admitted to the following tests" (written and oral) and section 7 that those who fail one session may re-apply for a later one. How written and oral results are combined into an admission decision, and whether any merit weighting applies, is therefore unknown from official sources. [uncertain]

SECOND-YEAR TRACK SELECTION (three curricula, chosen for year two): (1) "Hospitality and Tourism Management" at the University of Central Florida, Rosen College of Hospitality Management, Orlando (dual degree: Italian Laurea Magistrale + American M.Sc., with the possibility of staying in the US for a year of work in the tourism sector after graduation); (2) "Digital Technologies and Data for Tourism and Creative Industries" entirely at IULM Milan (Italian Laurea Magistrale only); (3) "Sustainable Destination Management and Communication", first semester at IULM Milan and second semester at the University of Oulu, Finland (dual degree: Italian Laurea Magistrale + Finnish M.Sc. in Geography, specialising in Tourism Geographies).

DUAL-DEGREE SUPPLEMENTARY REQUIREMENTS - UCF (section 6 of the admission regulations, the only track for which the regulations set out formal criteria): "TOEFL certification with a minimum score of 220 (computer-based) or 80 (internet-based), or IELTS certification with a minimum score of 6.5, obtained less than two years ago, or, if still to be taken, to be obtained preferably prior to enrolment in the first year and in any case no later than 30 November 2026"; "an average degree mark of at least 3.0 out of 4.0 on the GPA scale (which generally corresponds to an average mark of at least 27/30 on a first-cycle degree course when taking final examinations). The GPA certification must be obtained from the following body: WORLD EDUCATION SERVICES (WES) by 15 December 2026"; and first-year IULM exams in Hospitality and Service Management (6 CFU), Tourism Marketing (18 CFU), Human Resource Management in Tourism (6 CFU), Geography for Sustainable Tourism Development (9 CFU) and Accounting and Financial Management in Tourism (6 CFU) "passed with a mark of at least 26/30 (the equivalent of a grade B in accordance with an Agreement with UCF)". The English programme page instead summarises this last condition as "an average of no less than 26.5/30 in the first year at IULM" - see uncertainty_notes for this discrepancy.

DUAL-DEGREE SUPPLEMENTARY REQUIREMENTS - OULU: stated only on the English programme page, not in the admission regulations PDF: "TOEFL certificate with a score of 92 (with a minimum of 20 in the writing section)" or "IELTS certificate with a score of 6.5 (with a minimum of 5.5 in each section)". No GPA threshold, no first-year exam-mark threshold, no quota of dual-degree places and no separate application deadline for the Oulu mobility is published on iulm.it. [uncertain]

ASSESSMENT OF FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS: applications from holders of foreign qualifications are assessed individually by IULM's Admission Office, which "will carefully evaluate all the documentation submitted, check that the access requirements have been met" before the admission test. At enrolment, foreign-qualification holders must supply the qualification in the original language with an Italian translation where required, plus "documentation verifying the authenticity of the qualification, such as a Statement of Comparability and/or CIMEA verification, or a Dichiarazione di Valore (official statement issued by the Italian diplomatic authorities), as required by the University".

SPECIAL NEEDS: applicants with disabilities (Law 104/92), Specific Learning Disorders (Law 170/2010), ADHD or Autism must upload valid, legally compliant certification in PDF during the online test enrolment procedure, and must request dispensation and/or compensatory measures by e-mail to the diversaMENTE service (diversamente@iulm.it, tel. 02.891412200) before the test enrolment deadline.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH - minimum CEFR B2, and it is a gate to the admission test itself: "Only candidates, both internal and external, who have demonstrated proficiency in the English language to a level of not less than B2 will be admitted to the following tests". The same applies to foreign candidates. Proficiency is verified in one of four alternative ways (section 4 of the admission regulations, "Language requirement: English language proficiency to at least level B2"):
1. A language certificate obtained after 1 January 2024: IELTS with a score of at least 5.5; TOEFL iBT with a score of at least 87; Cambridge English with a score of at least 165.
2. A Bachelor's degree obtained (in Italy or abroad) on a course held in English.
3. Passing IULM's own Assessment Test (Oxford Placement Test), offered online at no extra cost to candidates who hold neither of the above, with a grade of at least level B2 in BOTH the Listening and Use of English sections - so IULM's own placement test fully substitutes for an external certificate.
4. Having already passed the IULM Assessment Test at B2 or above in both sections in an admissions session of a.y. 2025/26, and in any case not before 1 February 2025.
Candidates who do not meet the requirement when registering for the admission test are automatically placed on the Assessment Test list. Assessment Test dates for a.y. 2026/27: 1 December 2025 (session 1); 20 January and 25 February 2026 (session 2); 9 April and 28 April 2026 (session 3, "only if places still available or only for non-EU students"); 25 June 2026 (session 4, same condition); 4 September 2026 (session 5, per the general master's enrolment page; the programme regulations say only "dates to be defined only if places still available").
No exemption from the English requirement is granted to internal IULM candidates in this programme's regulations.

ENGLISH FOR THE DUAL-DEGREE TRACKS - HIGHER THAN THE IULM ENTRY LEVEL: the UCF second-year track requires TOEFL 220 computer-based / 80 internet-based, or IELTS 6.5, obtained less than two years earlier and in any case no later than 30 November 2026. The Oulu track requires TOEFL 92 with at least 20 in writing, or IELTS 6.5 with at least 5.5 in each section. Applicants intending to pursue a dual degree therefore need a materially higher English score than the IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 87 that suffices for admission to IULM itself, but these are second-year track conditions, not entry conditions.

ITALIAN - not an admission requirement, but a graduation requirement. "Candidates who are not native speakers of Italian and/or non-Italian citizens are required to declare their level of knowledge of the Italian language when applying for the admissions test, and they must obtain by the end of their course of studies the required qualification attesting to written and oral proficiency in Italian." Candidates are directed to the University's separately published "Procedures for the assessment and acquisition of knowledge of the Italian language". The general international-prerequisites page states that a CILS/CELI/PLIDA certificate at CEFR B2, or IULM's own online Italian assessment test, is required - but that statement applies expressly to Italian-taught courses, so the exact Italian level demanded for graduation from this English-taught programme is not confirmed. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu:
Academic year 2026/2027. Applications open 11 November 2025 ("From 11 November 2025 the following categories of candidates will be able to apply for admission following the online procedure"). Registration for session 1 opened 11 November 2025 at 10:00 a.m. and closed 25 November 2025 at 11:59 p.m.

Five sessions were held for this programme. Per session: [application deadline] -> [written test] -> [oral test] -> [enrolment confirmation deadline]
- Session 1: apply by 25 November 2025 -> written test 5 December 2025 -> oral test 9 December 2025 -> enrol by 15 January 2026.
- Session 2: apply by 19 February 2026 -> written test 4 March 2026 -> oral test 12 March 2026 -> enrol by 31 March 2026.
- Session 3: apply by 23 April 2026 ("only if places still available or only for non-EU students") -> written test 5 May 2026 -> oral test 11 May 2026 -> enrol by 4 June 2026.
- Extraordinary session (added after the regulations were issued; shown on the programme's registration pages but not in the admission regulations PDF): written test 4 June 2026 -> oral test 11 June 2026 per the English registration page (the Italian registration page shows 6 July 2026 for the oral - see uncertainty_notes). The general master's calendar gives an exceptional enrolment date of 29 June 2026.
- Session 4: registration open 22 May 2026 at 10:00 a.m. to 18 June 2026 at 11:59 p.m. -> written test 2 July 2026 -> oral test 6 July 2026 -> enrol by 28 July 2026.
- Session 5: registration open 30 June 2026 at 10:00 a.m. to 31 August 2026 at 11:59 p.m. -> written test 8 September 2026 -> oral test 11 September 2026 -> enrol by 18 September 2026.

IMPORTANT - THIS PROGRAMME DID NOT FILL EARLY. In contrast to Marketing, Consumer Behaviour and Communication (English) and Strategic Communication, which IULM declared "sold out" in its fourth- and fifth-session news items, Hospitality and Tourism Management was listed with live test dates in BOTH the fourth session (2 July 2026) and the fifth session ("Hospitality and Tourism Management: Written test September 8, 2026; Oral test September 11, 2026"). Places were therefore still available in September 2026, and the effective final EU application deadline for a.y. 2026/2027 was 31 August 2026.

Other rules: "The dates of the tests already scheduled are subject to changes, which will be communicated to the candidates in advance." "Depending on the number of admissions and the number of remaining places, the deadlines for enrolments may be shortened to allow the scrolling of the ranking list." Candidates who fail one session may apply for a later session without paying the EUR 110 fee again, subject to availability of places. Enrolment is confirmed only on payment of the first instalment. Candidates who do not yet hold a degree certificate are enrolled "conditionally" and must communicate the degree date and grade through the online services and upload the certificate no later than 31 December 2026, failing which the enrolment is officially annulled with no refund of the first instalment or the test fee. Internal IULM third-year students applying in session 2 have their a.y. 2025/26 third-instalment deadline deferred to 22 April 2026 (instead of 31 March). Teaching for a.y. 2026/27 starts 21 September 2026.
application_deadline_non_eu:
Non-EU applicants residing abroad apply through the dedicated international platform apply.iulm.it, not through the standard Italian online procedure. The international procedure page states that non-EU applicants living abroad can submit their application on apply.iulm.it "subject to availability of places" for the master's course concerned, "by the end of April" - so the nominal non-EU cut-off for a.y. 2026/2027 was the end of April 2026. In practice, because this programme still had places, IULM's regulations expressly reserve the later sessions to non-EU candidates: sessions 3, 4 and 5 are flagged "only if places still available or only for non-EU students", and the fifth-session written test was held on 8 September 2026.

Steps: (1) submit the application with all required documents on apply.iulm.it for an assessment of qualifications; (2) pay the application fee (apply.iulm.it lists "Application fee EUR 60 one-time"; the admission regulations separately set the admission test fee at EUR 110); (3) eligibility evaluation - IULM will "review your application and get back to you within approximately 15 working days"; (4) sit the online admission test (for foreign candidates: the closed-ended written test plus the uploaded video answers, see entry_exam_or_test); (5) receive the test outcome by e-mail; (6) complete enrolment through the University's Online Services; (7) pay the first tuition instalment to secure the place.

VISA / PRE-ENROLMENT: applicants must "submit a student visa application via Universitaly platform from March to the end of May" and lodge the pre-enrolment request with the Italian consular authorities.

FINAL ENROLMENT CUT-OFF FOR FOREIGN-QUALIFICATION HOLDERS: "Students holding a foreign qualification are required to complete the enrolment process no later than 31 January 2027 by submitting all documentation required for this purpose, including: a Type D study visa (where required); their tax code (codice fiscale); the admission qualification in the original language together with an Italian translation (where required); and documentation verifying the authenticity of the qualification, such as a Statement of Comparability and/or CIMEA verification, or a Dichiarazione di Valore." Failure to submit the required documentation by 31 January 2027 annuls the 2026/27 enrolment ex officio, "with no entitlement to a refund of any fees already paid".

REFUNDS: the first instalment "can be refunded solely and exclusively on production of official documentation from the relevant Consulate certifying failure to obtain a study visa".

STATUS AT TIME OF RESEARCH (6 September 2026): the apply.iulm.it record for the programme displays "Academic year 2026/27 - Application period has ended - Studies commence 21 Sept 2026". Unlike the Strategic Communication record, it carries NO message about full capacity; the application period simply closed at the end of the admission cycle.

entry_exam_or_test:
Restricted-access programme with a genuinely TWO-STAGE admission test - a written test followed, on a separate later date, by an oral test. This is confirmed by section 9 of the admission regulations and by the session calendars, which list a distinct "written test" (prova scritta) date and "oral test" (prova orale) date for every session.

FEE: EUR 110. "Registration for the test requires payment of a fee of EUR 110. All candidates, both internal and external, must apply for admission to the test and pay the corresponding fee (even those admitted directly). The test enrolment fee is not refundable under any circumstances (with the exception of failure to take the test due to the exhaustion of available places or at the behest of the University's governing bodies)." Failure to attend for any reason gives no right to reimbursement. "Non-payment of the participation fee or payment after the deadline set for each session will preclude admission to the test."

GATE: only candidates who have already demonstrated English at CEFR B2 or above (certificate, English-taught Bachelor's, or a pass in IULM's free online Assessment Test / Oxford Placement Test at B2+ in both the Listening and Use of English sections) are admitted to the two tests. Assessment Test dates: 1 Dec 2025; 20 Jan and 25 Feb 2026; 9 Apr and 28 Apr 2026; 25 Jun 2026; 4 Sep 2026 (session 5, per the general master's calendar).

STAGE 1 - WRITTEN TEST (Italian-qualification candidates): "written test in English comprising closed-ended questions and one open-ended question, aimed at assessing logical, critical and verbal reasoning skills, as well as testing basic knowledge regarding the disciplinary field of the degree course".

STAGE 2 - ORAL TEST (Italian-qualification candidates): "oral test aimed at assessing knowledge and skills; the Commissions for assessing personal preparation of the candidates will include at least two members besides the candidate".

FOREIGN CANDIDATES - MODIFIED TWO-STAGE FORMAT: holders of a foreign admission qualification sit a written test WITHOUT the open-ended question - "written test in English comprising closed-ended questions, aimed at assessing logical, critical and verbal reasoning skills, as well as testing basic knowledge regarding the disciplinary field of the degree course" - and, in place of the live oral interview, undergo "assessment of skills and knowledge by uploading onto the platform provided by the University (apply.iulm.it) videos related to the set questions". So the two stages are preserved for international applicants but the second stage is an asynchronous video submission rather than a live commission interview.

DELIVERY: "The tests will be carried out online." Duration, number of questions, marks available and the pass mark are not published for either stage. [uncertain]

RECOMMENDED BIBLIOGRAPHY FOR TEST PREPARATION (section 10 of the regulations), covering four subject areas: Business Administration - Sainaghi R., 2025, "Firm strategy and financial results", McGrawHill, Milano (chapters 1, 2, 5); Marketing - Kotler P., Keller K.L., 2016, "A Framework for Marketing Management", Pearson (chapters 1, 2, 3); Tourism - J. Fletcher, A. Fyall, D. Gilbert, S. Wanhill, 2017, "Tourism. Principles and Practice", 6th Edition, Pearson (chapters 1-3, 6-10, 13-14, 16-18); Territory - Nelson V., 2021, "An introduction to the geography of tourism", 3rd Edition, Rowman & Littlefield (chapters 1, 2, 7). "At the time of enrolment, texts or online courses may be recommended for all categories of candidates to follow before the start of the courses."

TEST DATES FOR a.y. 2026/2027 (written -> oral): session 1, 5 December 2025 -> 9 December 2025; session 2, 4 March 2026 -> 12 March 2026; session 3, 5 May 2026 -> 11 May 2026 (only if places still available or only for non-EU students); extraordinary session, 4 June 2026 -> 11 June 2026 (English registration page; the Italian page shows 6 July 2026 for the oral); session 4, 2 July 2026 -> 6 July 2026 (only if places still available or only for non-EU students); session 5, 8 September 2026 -> 11 September 2026. "The dates of the tests already scheduled are subject to changes, which will be communicated to the candidates in advance."

SCORING AND RANKING: not published. The regulations do not state how the written and oral results are weighted or combined, whether each stage has a separate pass threshold, whether the oral is only open to those who pass the written, or whether any merit points from the Bachelor's grade or exam average are added (other IULM master's programmes publish such a merit scale; this one does not). Candidates who fail one session may re-sit in a later session without paying the fee again, subject to availability of places. [uncertain]

uncertainty_notes:
YEAR COVERED: all figures are for academic year 2026/2027, taken from the programme-specific English admission regulations "Modalita ammissione LM HTM 2026_2027_ENG.pdf" (Faculty Board meeting 13/10/2025, revised Faculty Board meeting 3/3/2026), its Italian twin "Modalita ammissione LM HTM 2026_2027.pdf", and the 2026/2027 fee regulations (Rector's Decree no. 21472 of 27 November 2025). No 2025/2026 fallback was needed.

TWO-STAGE WRITTEN + ORAL TEST - CONFIRMED. Section 9 of the regulations sets out a written test in English (closed-ended questions plus one open-ended question, testing logical, critical and verbal reasoning plus basic disciplinary knowledge) followed by a separate oral test before a commission of at least two members, and every session calendar lists two distinct dates. Foreign-qualification candidates take a modified version: the written test WITHOUT the open-ended question, and instead of the live oral, they upload videos answering set questions to apply.iulm.it. Both stages are held online. This is the only IULM English-taught master's programme found in this research with a two-stage format.

PROGRAMME NOT FULL/CLOSED BEFORE THE FINAL SESSION - the opposite of what was seen for other IULM programmes. IULM's fourth- and fifth-session news items list Hospitality and Tourism Management with live test dates (2 July 2026, then written 8 September / oral 11 September 2026) while expressly naming Marketing, Consumer Behaviour and Communication (English) and Strategic Communication as sold out. Places therefore remained available through the fifth session, and the effective final application deadline for a.y. 2026/2027 was 31 August 2026 (enrolment by 18 September 2026). The apply.iulm.it record shows only "Application period has ended" for 2026/27, with no full-capacity message.

QUOTA DISCREPANCY CHECK - NONE FOUND. The English regulations PDF, the Italian regulations PDF, the English registration page and the Italian registration page all state 100 places for a.y. 2026/2027. The English/Italian quota mismatch observed elsewhere in this research does not occur for this programme.

RANKING CRITERIA COMPLETELY ABSENT - THE LARGEST GAP. Unlike the Strategic Communication regulations, which publish a detailed merit-point scale, per-session CFU thresholds, internal-candidate direct-admission quotas and tie-break rules, the Hospitality and Tourism Management regulations (checked in both language versions, all 5 pages, sections 1-13) contain NO ranking-list section at all. Unknown: how the written and oral scores are weighted or combined; whether each stage has its own pass mark; whether the oral is conditional on passing the written; whether Bachelor's degree grade or exam average contributes merit points; how many of the 100 places are allocated to each session; the tie-break rule; and whether internal Tourism, Management and Culture graduates enjoy any preferential route (they are listed as an eligible category but no exemption from the test is stated for them). Prospective applicants must contact ammissioni.magistrali@iulm.it for these rules.

TEST DURATION AND STRUCTURE NOT QUANTIFIED. Neither the number of closed-ended questions, the time allowed, the maximum score, nor the pass threshold is published for the written test; no duration or scoring rubric is published for the oral test or for the video submission. Only the four-subject recommended bibliography (Business Administration, Marketing, Tourism, Territory) indicates the topic coverage.

EXTRAORDINARY-SESSION DATE CONFLICT BETWEEN THE ENGLISH AND ITALIAN PAGES. Both registration pages show an extraordinary session that does not appear in either version of the regulations PDF. The English page (.../hospitality-tourism-management/iscrizioni) gives written test 4 June 2026 and oral test 11 June 2026; the Italian page (.../it/.../hospitality-tourism-management/iscrizioni) gives written test 04/06/26 but oral test 06/07/26 (6 July 2026), which is the same date as the fourth session's oral and looks like a data-entry error on the Italian page. The English date (11 June 2026) is reported above as the more plausible reading, but this could not be resolved from a third IULM source. The general master's enrolment calendar lists an "exceptional session" enrolment deadline of 29 June 2026, which is consistent with a June oral test.

UCF FIRST-YEAR MARK REQUIREMENT - REGULATIONS AND PROGRAMME PAGE DISAGREE. The admission regulations require five named first-year exams (Hospitality and Service Management 6 CFU, Tourism Marketing 18 CFU, Human Resource Management in Tourism 6 CFU, Geography for Sustainable Tourism Development 9 CFU, Accounting and Financial Management in Tourism 6 CFU) each to be "passed with a mark of at least 26/30". The English programme page instead summarises the condition as "an average of no less than 26.5/30 in the first year at IULM". These are different tests (a per-exam floor versus an overall average, and 26 versus 26.5). The regulations PDF, as the governing document, should be treated as authoritative; the discrepancy is flagged here because the programme page is the more visible source.

OULU TRACK REQUIREMENTS PUBLISHED ONLY ON THE PROGRAMME PAGE. Section 6 of the regulations sets out supplementary requirements for the UCF track ONLY. The Oulu (Sustainable Destination Management and Communication) requirements - TOEFL 92 with at least 20 in writing, or IELTS 6.5 with at least 5.5 in each section - appear only on the English programme page, with no GPA threshold, no first-year exam-mark threshold, no WES-equivalent credential-evaluation step, no deadline for producing the certificate, and no quota of Oulu places. Whether a further Oulu-side selection exists is not stated on any iulm.it page. Likewise, no quota or internal-selection rule is published for the UCF places, so it is unknown whether meeting the stated thresholds guarantees the dual-degree place or merely qualifies a student to compete for it.

APPLY.IULM.IT DOCUMENT LIST NOT PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC. The apply.iulm.it record for this programme (course 57) states the entry qualification, the English requirement and the fees, but - unlike the Strategic Communication record - it does not display a "Specific requirements" block naming the motivation letter, reference letter or Universitaly visa step. Those items are listed generically on the international procedure page and have been carried into required_documents on that basis; they were not confirmed on a page specific to this programme. The apply.iulm.it pages return HTTP 403 to WebFetch and were read via a direct HTTP request on 6 September 2026. Note the platform also carries a separate legacy record "MA International Tourism and Hospitality" (course 36) - the current record for this programme is course 57.

ITALIAN-LANGUAGE GRADUATION REQUIREMENT NOT QUANTIFIED. The regulations require non-native-Italian speakers to obtain "by the end of their course of studies the required qualification attesting to written and oral proficiency in Italian" and refer to a separate document, "Procedures for the assessment and acquisition of knowledge of the Italian language", which was not retrieved. The CEFR level and accepted certificates for that graduation requirement are therefore unknown; the CILS/CELI/PLIDA B2 standard on the general international-prerequisites page applies expressly to Italian-taught courses.

FEE FIGURES. The linked fee PDF covers students whose family resides abroad (single contribution band): for a first-year master's student, EUR 10,806 total (enrolment fee 250 + regional tax 206 + student services 90 + university fee 10,260), payable as EUR 2,000 first instalment plus EUR 146 regional tax advance on enrolment, EUR 5,300 plus EUR 60 regional tax balance by 14/12/2026, and EUR 3,300 by 31/03/2027 - matching the EUR 10,806 per year shown on apply.iulm.it. A reduced band of EUR 4,646 total applies to students from developing countries listed in Ministerial Decree no. 166/2025. Students assessed on an Italian ISEE pay according to the separate general fee regulations, which were not extracted. Late payments incur a EUR 50 penalty (under EUR 3,000) or EUR 100 (above). No tuition figure is published on iulm.it for the second year spent at UCF or Oulu, and whether partner-university fees apply is not stated.
